lines.trans: Hello, sir—would you like to come inside for a warm cup of tea?
Wait... our old neighbour from the violin shop at number ten?!
You two know each other, Manager Zhou?!
Thirty years ago, every Friday evening at six, he brought his violin here!
Wait—look at our old postcard: "Please save two chairs for the baker and the teacher"!
He was the music teacher who played Friday duets with your aunt back then!
He just asked me who on earth finally finished the second half of her May waltz!
What did he say when he heard my sixteen bars through the window, Manager Zhou?
He had tears in his eyes—he said it sounded just like my aunt's voice!
Did you invite him to join our grand opening this Friday evening at six o'clock?!
He promised to bring his violin over—and ten old neighbours from down the street!
Ten extra neighbours?! By Friday, Mei is going to need twice as many yellow lemons!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yī. Changes tone to yí before 4th tone (一个 yí gè) and yì before 1st/2nd/3rd tones (一杯 yì bēi).

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

meanings.note: Pinyin: sān shí. Cardinal number thirty ('three tens'); pairs directly with measure words like 三十年 ('thirty years').

examples.text: 这棵老树在院子里长了三十年。
examples.trans: This old tree has grown in the courtyard for thirty years.

examples.text: 从客栈走到地铁站只要三十分钟。
examples.trans: Walking from the inn to the metro station takes only thirty minutes.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shàng. Used both as a directional verb/complement ('up, onto') and location word ('on top of').

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

examples.text: 不要太着急了，招聘竞争都很激烈。
examples.trans: Do not get too anxious; the hiring competition is very fierce.

examples.text: 这是不要。
examples.trans: This is 不要.

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎng. Used instead of 二 when counting things with a measure word (两个, 两把, 两间).

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gè. Most common Mandarin measure word (量词), placed between a number/demonstrative and a noun (一个人, 这个).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 刚烤好的面包卷！趁热拿一个吧。
examples.trans: Freshly baked bread rolls! Take one while it is hot.

meanings.note: Pinyin: le. After a verb, marks completion; at the end of a sentence, signals a change of situation.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

meanings.note: Pinyin: èr chóng zòu. Measure word (量词): 首, e.g. 一首二重奏 ('a duet piece').

examples.text: 生活安排的二重奏比我们自己写得更妙，孩子们。
examples.trans: Life arranges finer duets than we write ourselves, boys.

examples.text: 老师和学生一起弹了一首欢快的钢琴二重奏。
examples.trans: Teacher and student played a cheerful piano duet together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǔ yuè. Fifth month of the year ('month five').

examples.text: 五月的成都院子里到处都是花香。
examples.trans: In May, courtyards in Chengdu are filled with the scent of flowers everywhere.

examples.text: 这张旧照片是五月的一个晴天拍的。
examples.trans: This old photo was taken on a sunny day in May.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shén me. Asks 'what?' on its own (什么？) or modifies a noun (什么茶 'what kind of tea').

examples.text: 太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
examples.trans: Great. Please tell me what I need to know.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

meanings.note: Pinyin: tā. Third-person singular masculine pronoun; pronounced identically to 她 and 它.

examples.text: 他没要回那个装木头小火车的箱子吗？
examples.trans: Did he not ask back for that case with the wooden train?

examples.text: 他留了纸条，请我们保管到星期五。
examples.trans: He left a note asking us to keep it until Friday.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wèi. Polite counterpart of 个 when counting guests, customers, or teachers (一位客人, 这位老师).

examples.text: 太谢谢你们两位了。
examples.trans: Thank you both so very much.

examples.text: 七点半有八位饿肚子的客人下楼啊！
examples.trans: At seven thirty, eight hungry guests are coming downstairs!

meanings.note: Pinyin: nǐ men. Plural 'you' for addressing two or more people (including polite groups).

examples.text: 太谢谢你们两位了。
examples.trans: Thank you both so very much.

examples.text: 不怪你们。只是我身上只有这件外套！
examples.trans: It is not your fault. Still, I only have this one coat on me!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liǎ. Colloquial fusion of 两个, never followed by 个 (我们俩 'the two of us').

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

examples.text: 别动，你们俩。听到路边汽车停下的声音了吗？
examples.trans: Hold still, both of you. Hear that car engine stopping at the curb?

meanings.note: Pinyin: bàng wǎn. Combines 傍 ('draw near to') + 晚 ('evening'): the golden hour around sunset.

examples.text: 傍晚的时候，院子里的灯笼一盏接一盏亮了。
examples.trans: At dusk, the lanterns in the courtyard lit up one after another.

examples.text: 夏天的傍晚最适合坐在院子里乘凉。
examples.trans: Summer evenings at dusk are perfect for sitting in the courtyard to enjoy the breeze.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiān sheng. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位先生 ('a gentleman').

examples.text: 等等——先生您好！您问那个深蓝色行李箱吗？
examples.trans: Wait—hello, sir! Are you asking about that dark-blue suitcase?

examples.text: 先生，箱子安全锁在柜子里。请问您贵姓？
examples.trans: Sir, the bag is locked safely in our closet. May I ask your surname?

meanings.note: Pinyin: quán. Emphasizes entirety before 都 or a verb (全都 'every single one').

examples.text: 怪不得这么重，全是木头和皮鞋！
examples.trans: No wonder it was so heavy—all wood and leather shoes!

examples.text: 四张桌子，八把椅子，全摆好了！
examples.trans: Four tables, eight chairs—everything is set in place!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liù. Cardinal number 6.

examples.text: 老陈……小晴……快告诉我今晚六号房空着。
examples.trans: Chen... Qing... please tell me room six is free tonight.

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zài jiàn. Standard Mandarin farewell at any time of day.

examples.text: 路上小心，我们明天再见！
examples.trans: Take care on the road—see you again tomorrow!

examples.text: 谢谢您的帮忙，再见！
examples.trans: Thank you for your help—goodbye!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiě. Used for writing characters, notes, letters, or reviews.

examples.text: 到星期五？没写名字，也没签名！
examples.trans: Until Friday? No name written, and no signature either!

examples.text: 只剩三十五分钟了！他肯定会写一星差评！
examples.trans: Only thirty-five minutes left! He will surely write a one-star bad review!

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiě wán. Resultative verb compound 写 ('write') + 完 ('finish').

examples.text: 宋老师终于在傍晚前写完了整首圆舞曲。
examples.trans: Teacher Song finally finished writing the whole waltz before dusk.

examples.text: 我写完这张明信片就去邮局寄出。
examples.trans: As soon as I finish writing this postcard, I will mail it at the post office.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhǔn bèi. Used for preparing rooms, breakfast, or plans.

examples.text: 大家早上好！欢迎你，小晴。都准备好了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone! Welcome, Qing. Is everything ready?

examples.text: 周经理早！桌子很干净，钥匙也准备好了。
examples.trans: Morning, Manager Zhou! The desk is clean, and the keys are ready too.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gāng cái. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 刚才那一刻 ('that moment just now').

examples.text: 谢谢你，小美。刚才吓了一跳，手都凉了！
examples.trans: Thank you, Mei. That gave me such a start just now that my hands went cold!

examples.text: 您刚才忘在楼下前台汤碗旁边了。
examples.trans: You left it downstairs beside the soup bowl at the front desk.

related.gloss: that moment just now (measure word 个)

meanings.note: Pinyin: dào. Works as main verb ('arrive') or result complement ('succeed in reaching/perceiving', 找到, 听到).

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: dào dǐ. Adds urgent curiosity inside a question (到底在哪儿？ 'where on earth is it?').

examples.text: 老弟，你到底撞进了一家什么神奇客栈？
examples.trans: Little brother, what kind of magical inn did you stumble into?

examples.text: 这家客栈向来只有八间客房！九号房到底在哪儿？！
examples.trans: This inn has only ever had eight guest rooms! Where on earth is Room Nine?!

meanings.note: Pinyin: qián. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个前面 ('a front side').

examples.text: 二十五年前我在附近教钢琴，不过记忆淡了。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano nearby, though memories fade.

examples.text: 没有啊，周经理，南方来的夫妻一小时前住进六号房了。
examples.trans: No, Manager Zhou, the couple from the south checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí. Cardinal number 10; building block for 11–99.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shí liù. Cardinal number 十 ('ten') + 六 ('six').

examples.text: 这首圆舞曲最后还缺少十六个小节。
examples.trans: This waltz is still missing sixteen bars at the end.

examples.text: 茶壶里泡的薄荷茶够倒十六小杯。
examples.trans: The mint tea steeped in the teapot is enough to pour sixteen small cups.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yuán lái. Marks an 'aha!' discovery ('so it was X all along!').

examples.text: 原来星期五的神秘客人一直睡在我阁楼屋顶下面。
examples.trans: So our mystery Friday caller was sleeping under my attic roof all along.

examples.text: 原来留着爷爷旧物的神秘人一直是你，志豪。
examples.trans: So the mystery person holding Grandfather's keepsake was you all along, Zhihao.

meanings.note: Verb cānjiā.

examples.text: 她参加我们的节目。
examples.trans: She joins our show.

examples.text: 明天谁参加会议？
examples.trans: Who is attending tomorrow's meeting?

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuāng bèi. Combines 双 ('double/two') + 倍 ('times/fold'); used before nouns with 的 or after verbs.

examples.text: 既然星期五要多来十位老街坊，小美得准备双倍的黄柠檬啦！
examples.trans: Since ten extra neighbours are coming on Friday, Mei will need to prepare double the yellow lemons!

examples.text: 周末客栈客人多，我们今天揉了双倍的面团。
examples.trans: Because the inn has many guests on weekends, we kneaded double the dough today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiào. Introduces a person's given or full name (我叫小晴 'My name is Xiaoqing') or calls a cab.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.note: Pinyin: hào. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个号码 ('a number').

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

合奏.gloss: play music together; perform in ensemble

meanings.en: play music together; perform in ensemble
meanings.note: Pinyin: hé zòu. Combines 合 ('join together') + 奏 ('play music'); also used as a noun for an instrumental ensemble.

examples.text: 他就是当年每个星期五跟您姑姑合奏的音乐老师！
examples.trans: He is the very music teacher who used to play Friday duets with your aunt back then!

examples.text: 小提琴和核桃木钢琴在阳光房里合奏出温暖的旋律。
examples.trans: The violin and the walnut piano played a warm melody together in the sunroom.

后半段.gloss: second half (of a song, road, or event)

meanings.en: second half (of a song, road, or event)
meanings.note: Pinyin: hòu bàn duàn. Combines 后 ('back/latter') + 半 ('half') + 段 ('section/stretch').

examples.text: 这首曲子的后半段比开头更温柔。
examples.trans: The second half of this piece is gentler than the opening.

examples.text: 电影的后半段让大家都看入迷了。
examples.trans: The second half of the film captivated everyone.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ma. Placed at the end of any statement to turn it into a neutral yes/no question.

examples.text: 早上好！请问，门锁了吗？
examples.trans: Good morning! Excuse me, is the door locked?

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: tīng jiàn. Result compound: 听 ('listen') + 见 ('perceive') = 'actually hear'.

examples.text: 没错。外面大街很吵，进了院子却只听见树叶和小鸟。
examples.trans: Exactly. Outside on the main road it is noisy, yet inside the courtyard you only hear leaves and birds.

examples.text: 关上木窗就听不见外面的车声了。
examples.trans: Close the wooden window and you cannot hear the street traffic.

examples.text: 在冷雨里走了一路，喝碗热汤听起来太棒了。
examples.trans: After walking all the way in the cold rain, having a bowl of hot soup sounds wonderful.

examples.text: 你的这个主意听起来既省钱又实用。
examples.trans: Your idea sounds both economical and practical.

meanings.note: Pinyin: ya. Gentle exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

examples.text: 呀，这就是星期一火车上那只双胞胎箱子吗？
examples.trans: Oh, is this that twin suitcase from Monday's train?

meanings.note: Pinyin: hé. Joins nouns or pronouns ('A and B'), NEVER two whole clauses; also means 'with' (和你一样).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: la. Colloquial fusion of 了 + 啊 adding cheerful energy at the end of a sentence.

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 你们守着，我出门啦！
examples.trans: Hold the fort—I am heading out the door!

meanings.note: Pinyin: hē. Used for drinking tea, coffee, water, juice, AND soup in Mandarin (喝汤).

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 我还没喝早咖啡呢，千万别说急事！
examples.trans: I have not had my morning coffee yet; please do not say emergency!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yuán wǔ qǔ. Compound from 圆 ('circle') + 舞 ('dance') + 曲 ('musical piece'). Measure word: 首 (shǒu).

examples.text: 宋老师在钢琴上弹了一首轻快的圆舞曲。
examples.trans: Teacher Song played a lively waltz on the piano.

examples.text: 这首老圆舞曲让人想起三十年前的晚茶会。
examples.trans: This old waltz brings back memories of evening tea gatherings thirty years ago.

meanings.note: Pinyin: shēng yīn. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个声音 ('a voice / sound').

examples.text: 声音客气吗？年轻人还是老人？
examples.trans: Was the voice polite? A young person or an older person?

examples.text: 声音轻，很有礼貌，大概三十多岁，有点紧张。
examples.trans: Soft-spoken, very polite, around thirty-something, and a bit nervous.

meanings.note: Pinyin: duō. Means 'many' as an adjective, 'how…?' before adjectives (多大), or 'more than' after round numbers (三十多).

examples.text: 声音轻，很有礼貌，大概三十多岁，有点紧张。
examples.trans: Soft-spoken, very polite, around thirty-something, and a bit nervous.

examples.text: 说实话，我比以前灰色办公室喜欢这儿多了。
examples.trans: Honestly, I like this place far better than my old grey office.

meanings.note: Pinyin: tā. Third-person singular feminine pronoun; written with the woman radical 女.

examples.text: 看拉链旁边……对，有她的名字缩写！
examples.trans: Check beside the zipper... yes, her name initials are here!

examples.text: 等等——星期一你们坐同一班火车，并拿走了她的箱子？
examples.trans: Wait—so you rode the same train on Monday and took her suitcase?

meanings.note: Pinyin: gū gu. Specifically father's sister (second syllable neutral tone); distinct from 阿姨 / 姨妈 (mother's sister).

examples.text: 周经理的姑姑以前也住在这座老院子里。
examples.trans: Manager Zhou's paternal aunt used to live in this old courtyard too.

examples.text: 我姑姑年轻的时候最喜欢弹钢琴。
examples.trans: When my aunt was young, she loved playing the piano most of all.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎo tí qín. Combines 小 ('small') + 提 ('hold/carry in hand') + 琴 ('stringed instrument'); measure word: 把 (bǎ).

examples.text: 三十年前，每个星期五傍晚他都带着一把小提琴来九号房。
examples.trans: Thirty years ago, every Friday evening he brought a violin to Room Nine.

examples.text: 老先生答应星期五带上小提琴，和宋老师的钢琴一起合奏。
examples.trans: The elderly gentleman promised to bring his violin on Friday and play a duet with Teacher Song's piano.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xiǎo jié. In music notation, counts bars/measures between vertical barlines (二十四小节 'twenty-four bars').

examples.text: 这首圆舞曲的前八个小节特别轻快。
examples.trans: The opening eight bars of this waltz are especially light and lively.

examples.text: 宋老师用铅笔在第四小节旁边做了记号。
examples.trans: Teacher Song made a pencil mark beside the fourth bar.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù xiàng. Introduces a vivid comparison.

examples.text: 每天服务街坊邻居——就像对公众开放的早间咖啡馆？！
examples.trans: Serves neighbours daily—like a morning café open to the public?!

examples.text: 住在这里就像回到自己家一样舒服。
examples.trans: Staying here feels just as cozy as coming home.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù shì. Adds emphatic certainty before a noun ('is the very one').

examples.text: 你好！你就是小晴吧？我是厨房的小美。
examples.trans: Hello! You must be Qing, right? I am Mei from the kitchen.

examples.text: 没关系！您就是志豪先生吧？
examples.trans: No problem at all! You must be Mr Zhihao, right?

meanings.note: Pinyin: dài. Used for carrying keys, tools, or luggage with you.

examples.text: 这么快就修好了？老陈你随身带着螺丝刀啊！
examples.trans: Fixed that fast? Chen, you carry a screwdriver everywhere on you!

examples.text: 说实话，我选这一带，也是为了一桩家里的旧事。
examples.trans: Honestly, I also chose this neighbourhood for an old family matter.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nián. Time classifier taking no 个 directly after numbers (六年 'six years', 今年 'this year').

examples.text: 二十五年前我在附近教钢琴，不过记忆淡了。
examples.trans: Twenty-five years ago I taught piano nearby, though memories fade.

examples.text: 老橡木，八十年了，一滴水都不漏。
examples.trans: Old oak, eighty years old—not a single drop leaks.

meanings.note: Pinyin: diàn. Measure word (量词): 家 (jiā), e.g. 一家店 ('a shop / inn').

examples.text: 完全正确！目前你们四张桌子只接待住店客人。
examples.trans: Exactly right! Right now your four tables only serve overnight inn guests.

examples.text: 这条街上有好几家小店。
examples.trans: There are several small shops along this street.

开业.gloss: open for business; hold a grand opening

meanings.en: open for business; hold a grand opening
meanings.note: Pinyin: kāi yè. Separable verb-object compound 开 ('open/start') + 业 ('business/trade'); also used as a noun after modifiers (正式开业 'grand opening').

examples.text: 您邀请那位老先生来参加我们星期五傍晚六点的正式开业了吗？
examples.trans: Did you invite that elderly gentleman to come to our grand opening this Friday at six?

examples.text: 街坊们听说九号房咖啡馆要开业，纷纷停下来看门外的木牌。
examples.trans: Hearing that the Room Nine café was opening for business, neighbours stopped to read the wooden sign outside.

meanings.note: Time noun dāngnián ('in bygone years, back then').

examples.text: 当年他离开卫视时得罪了不少人。
examples.trans: Back when he left the network, he offended many people.

examples.text: 她想起当年刚进大学时的梦想。
examples.trans: She recalled her dreams from her freshman days.

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Read de after a verb to introduce how it goes (走得快 'walk fast'); read děi before a verb to mean 'must'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: kuài. As an adjective/adverb, 'fast/quickly'; in 快…了, 'about to'.

examples.text: 第一天上班，我走得快。电脑在哪里？
examples.trans: On my first day at work, I walk fast. Where is the computer?

examples.text: 小晴，快看里面！这不是我的箱子！
examples.trans: Qing, look inside quickly! This is not my case!

meanings.note: Pinyin: nín. Respectful singular 'you' used with elders, teachers, and guests (您好！).

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

examples.text: 就在您额头上，安全得很。
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, completely safe.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nín hǎo. Respectful greeting using polite 您 ('you') for elders, teachers, and guests.

examples.text: 您好，欢迎来到小院客栈！
examples.trans: Hello, welcome to Courtyard Inn!

examples.text: 老师您好，请进屋喝杯热茶。
examples.trans: Hello, Teacher—please come inside for a cup of hot tea.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ. First-person singular pronoun; add 的 for 'my' (我的) and 们 for 'we/us' (我们).

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 我叫老陈。你早到了十分钟。
examples.trans: I'm called Chen. You arrived ten minutes early.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wǒ men. First-person plural pronoun; add 的 for 'our' (我们的).

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

meanings.en: measure word for handled objects; disposal marker
meanings.note: Pinyin: bǎ. Counts items with handles or backs (一把钥匙, 一把椅子); as a preposition, fronts a definite object before an action verb.

examples.text: 早上好。没锁，先把把手往上提，再推。
examples.trans: Good morning. Not locked; lift the handle up first, then push.

examples.text: 对，八间客房，八把铜钥匙。四号房的客人今天到。
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiù. Describes old houses, pipes, or letters—never a person's age (use 老 for people).

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 不在，只有我的笔和三张旧收据！
examples.trans: Not there—only my pen and three old receipts!

meanings.note: Pinyin: míng xìn piàn. Measure word (量词): 张 (zhāng), e.g. 一张明信片 ('a postcard').

examples.text: 从那天起我们就再没说过话。上周我给他寄了一张明信片。
examples.trans: Since that day we have not spoken again. Last week I mailed him a postcard.

examples.text: 看，已经十二点零四分了。也许他把明信片扔进垃圾桶了。
examples.trans: Look, it is twelve-oh-four already. Maybe he tossed the postcard into the bin.

meanings.note: Pinyin: xīng qī wǔ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 每个星期五 ('every Friday').

examples.text: 我念念：对不起拿错了，请帮我保管到星期五。
examples.trans: Let me read it: Sorry for taking the wrong one; please keep mine until Friday.

examples.text: 到星期五？没写名字，也没签名！
examples.trans: Until Friday? No name written, and no signature either!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shì. Links two nouns (我是小晴); do NOT use simple 是 before plain adjectives like 好 or 忙.

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 有道理！这些是钥匙吗？
examples.trans: Fair enough! Are these the keys?

meanings.note: Pinyin: lái. Movement toward the speaker, as main verb or directional complement (进来 'come in').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 大门口正好来了一辆出租车。
examples.trans: A taxi has just pulled up right at the front gate.

杯.gloss: measure word for cups and glasses

meanings.en: measure word for cups and glasses
meanings.note: Pinyin: bēi. Counts cups of tea, coffee, water, or juice (一杯热茶 'a cup of hot tea').

examples.text: 太客气了，周经理。半杯就好。
examples.trans: How polite of you, Manager Zhou. Half a glass is fine.

examples.text: 坐下吧，小晴！早上你跑了半条街，喝杯咖啡。
examples.trans: Sit down, Qing! You ran half the street this morning—drink a cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Pinyin: níng méng. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 一个柠檬 ('a lemon').

examples.text: 他爷爷会切热柠檬蛋糕，上面撒一层白糖粉！
examples.trans: His grandfather sliced warm lemon cake with a dusting of powdered sugar on top!

examples.text: 啊！黄色柠檬糖霜——每个星期五我们俩都抢边角那一块！
examples.trans: Oh! Yellow lemon glaze—every single Friday the two of us fought over the corner piece!

meanings.note: Pinyin: yǐ zi. Measure word (量词): 把 (bǎ), e.g. 一把椅子 ('a chair').

examples.text: 四张桌子，八把椅子，全摆好了！
examples.trans: Four tables, eight chairs—everything is set in place!

examples.text: 当心那把角落椅子，等十秒我拧紧螺丝。
examples.trans: Mind that corner chair—wait ten seconds while I tighten the screw.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèng shì. Describes formal speech or a permanent job after probation.

examples.text: 我一紧张，句子就变得又长又正式！
examples.trans: Whenever I get nervous, my sentences turn long and formal!

examples.text: 周经理，要是你不正式聘用她，我就请她进我厨房！
examples.trans: Manager Zhou, if you do not hire her permanently, I am hiring her into my kitchen!

examples.text: 外卡？每个导师确实有个外卡名额，但是你之前已经放弃了。
examples.trans: A wild card? Every mentor does get one wild-card spot, except you already waived yours earlier.

examples.text: 这件事我们再商量一下。
examples.trans: Let's discuss this matter a bit more.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lèi shuǐ. Combines 泪 ('tears') + 水 ('water/liquid'), slightly more poetic and vivid than everyday 眼泪.

examples.text: 老先生眼眶里全是泪水，说这琴声听起来就像周经理的姑姑。
examples.trans: The older gentleman's eyes were full of tears as he said the piano sounded just like Manager Zhou's aunt.

examples.text: 听到失传三十年的旋律重新响起，大家都忍不住擦了擦感动的泪水。
examples.trans: Hearing the melody that had been lost for thirty years ring out again, everyone wiped away tears of emotion.

meanings.note: Pinyin: diǎn. Marks hours on the clock (八点 'eight o'clock') or 'a bit' (一点).

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

examples.text: 晚上九点？等等，我们一起去开大门。
examples.trans: At nine o'clock? Wait, let us open the gate together.

meanings.note: Pinyin: rè. Describes hot tea, hot water, or warm weather.

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 因为好咖啡和热面包让人开心呀！
examples.trans: Because good coffee and warm bread make people happy!

meanings.note: Pinyin: liú. Used for leaving a note/keepsake, saving food, or staying on (留下来).

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 为什么把鞋和木头小火车留到星期五呢？
examples.trans: Why leave the shoes and little wooden train here until Friday?

meanings.note: Pinyin: de. Links modifiers or owners to nouns (我的书 'my book', 安静的院子 'quiet courtyard').

examples.text: 啊，开了！谢谢。我是小晴，新来的前台。
examples.trans: Oh, it opened! Thank you. I am Qing, the new receptionist.

examples.text: 纸本子？真的吗？
examples.trans: A paper notebook? Really?

meanings.note: Pinyin: kàn. Covers looking at something, reading silently, or visiting someone; add 见/到 for 'catch sight of'.

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

examples.text: 老板，看一下桌子后面的镜子。
examples.trans: Boss, take a look in the mirror behind the desk.

眼眶.gloss: eye socket; rim of the eye

meanings.en: eye socket; rim of the eye
meanings.note: Pinyin: yǎn kuàng. Combines 眼 ('eye') + 眶 ('frame/socket of the eye'), frequently used in descriptions of emotion (眼眶湿润 'eyes brimming with tears').

examples.text: 听见窗里传出的十六个小节，老先生眼眶里全是泪水。
examples.trans: Hearing the sixteen bars drifting through the window, the older gentleman's eyes filled with tears.

examples.text: 周经理看着那枚蓝色的保护印章，眼眶也一下子红了。
examples.trans: Looking at that round blue heritage stamp, Manager Zhou's eyes grew misty too.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhe. Placed right after a verb to show a state or posture continues (门开着 'the door stands open').

examples.text: 就算四号房空着，旧电线也会响两下。
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire still rings twice.

examples.text: 白纸包着什么？一个木头小火车！
examples.trans: What is wrapped in white paper? A little wooden train!

meanings.note: Pinyin: chuāng hu. Measure word (量词): 扇 (shàn), e.g. 一扇窗户 ('a window').

examples.text: 太好了。窗户朝街上还是朝院子？
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

examples.text: 哇，看这间房！大木头房梁，窗户正对着院子！
examples.trans: Wow, look at this room! Big wooden beams, and a window facing the courtyard!

meanings.note: Pinyin: děng deng. Urgent or casual reduplication of 等 ('wait!').

examples.text: 等等，深蓝色的，跟您的一样啊！
examples.trans: Wait—it is dark blue, the same as yours!

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

meanings.note: Pinyin: dā ying. Means agreeing to a request or giving one's word.

examples.text: 让我猜猜，你把没有的房间答应给别人了？
examples.trans: Let me guess: you promised someone a room we do not have?

examples.text: 既然答应了别人，就一定要准时做到。
examples.trans: Once you give someone your word, be sure to follow through on time.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiǎn zhí. Emphatic adverb expressing enthusiastic amazement (简直无敌了 'simply unbeatable!').

examples.text: 杏仁挞底配上新鲜柠檬，味道简直无敌了！
examples.trans: Almond crust paired with fresh lemon is simply unbeatable!

examples.text: 擦亮玻璃后的阳光房简直像变了一间新屋子。
examples.trans: With the glass polished bright, the sunroom looks practically like a brand-new room.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhōng yú. Expresses relief or accomplishment when something long awaited happens.

examples.text: 把大难题分成三件小事，周经理终于能松口气了！
examples.trans: With the big problem divided into three small jobs, Manager Zhou could finally breathe again!

examples.text: 锁了三十年的木头窗板今天终于重新打开了。
examples.trans: The wooden shutters locked for thirty years finally swung open again today.

meanings.note: Pinyin: gěi. As main verb, 'give'; as preposition/complement, marks the recipient (给你 'for/to you', 递给我 'pass to me').

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 给您四号钥匙。早餐从七点半到十点。
examples.trans: Here is key number four for you. Breakfast is from seven thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǎo. Describes longtime friends, historic lanes, or warm respect before a colleague's surname (老陈).

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

examples.text: 所以老房子自己会打招呼？
examples.trans: So the old house says hello by itself?

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǎo shī. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位老师 ('a teacher').

examples.text: 是的，宋老师，二楼四号房！坐火车累吗？
examples.trans: Yes, Teacher Song, room four on the second floor! Was the train ride tiring?

examples.text: 宋老师，怎么了？您按了门铃！
examples.trans: Teacher Song, what happened? You rang the bell!

meanings.note: Pinyin: chá. Measure word (量词): 杯 (bēi), e.g. 一杯茶 ('a cup of tea').

examples.text: 第一条规矩：先喝热茶，再去开门。
examples.trans: Rule number one: drink hot tea first, then go answer the door.

examples.text: 先喝杯热茶，吃个肉桂卷坐十分钟吧！
examples.trans: Have a cup of hot tea and a cinnamon roll for ten minutes first!

related.gloss: a cup of tea (measure word 杯)

meanings.note: Pinyin: jiē. Measure word (量词): 条 (tiáo), e.g. 一条街 ('a street').

examples.text: 可惜没有电话号码，只有两个字母和老街名字。
examples.trans: Unfortunately there is no phone number, only two letters and an old street name.

examples.text: 等等，这条街就在附近，走过去只要五分钟！
examples.trans: Wait—that street is right nearby, only five minutes on foot!

meanings.en: neighbors; folks on the same street
meanings.note: Pinyin: jiē fang. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位街坊 ('a neighborhood resident').

examples.text: 超过八十年的小院建筑，只要一楼每天服务街坊邻居，禁止改成私人办公室。
examples.trans: Any courtyard building over eighty years old may not become private offices as long as the ground floor serves neighbours daily.

examples.text: 每天服务街坊邻居——就像对公众开放的早间咖啡馆？！
examples.trans: Serves neighbours daily—like a morning café open to the public?!

meanings.en: want; need; will / be going to
meanings.note: Pinyin: yào. Direct verb for ordering/requesting ('want'), obligation ('need to'), or imminent future (要下雨了).

examples.text: 今天四号房的客人住一整个星期，一定要完美！
examples.trans: Today's guest in room four is staying a whole week; everything must be perfect!

examples.text: 我要看预订本子，可是找不到我的眼镜了！
examples.trans: I need to read the booking ledger, yet I cannot find my glasses!

meanings.note: Pinyin: rèn shi. Contrast 知道 ('know a fact').

examples.text: 你好，小美，很高兴认识你！好香啊！
examples.trans: Hello, Mei, nice to meet you! Something smells wonderful!

examples.text: 真的吗？您在成都认识什么人吗？
examples.trans: Really? Do you know someone here in Chengdu?

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuō. Most common verb of speaking.

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 我还没喝早咖啡呢，千万别说急事！
examples.trans: I have not had my morning coffee yet; please do not say emergency!

meanings.note: Pinyin: qǐng. At the start of a request, means 'please' (请进, 请坐, 请问); before a person, 'invite / treat'.

examples.text: 太好了。请告诉我需要知道什么。
examples.trans: Great. Please tell me what I need to know.

examples.text: 还没有吗？请记下我们客栈的电话和地址，谢谢！
examples.trans: Not yet? Please write down our inn's phone number and address, thank you!

meanings.note: Pinyin: shuí. Question pronoun for people; stays in the exact spot of the answer (这是谁的？ 'Whose is this?').

examples.text: 谁也别说出去！门铃响的时候要微笑。
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone! Smile warmly when the bell rings.

examples.text: 一点没破！是谁送回来的？
examples.trans: Not cracked at all! Who brought it back?

meanings.note: Pinyin: gēn. As a verb, 'follow' (跟我来 'follow me'); as a preposition, 'with' (跟你一样 'same as yours').

examples.text: 跟我当然啦！客气话留给客人吧。
examples.trans: With me, of course! Save the polite talk for the guests.

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: guò lái. Directional compound moving across toward the speaker.

examples.text: 你看，早餐忙乱和神秘电话你都挺过来了！
examples.trans: Look, you made it through both the breakfast rush and the mystery phone call!

examples.text: 因为星期一晚上我走过来时，看见我哥哥正走在这条街上！
examples.trans: Because when I walked here Monday night, I saw my older brother walking down this street!

examples.text: 感觉非常好，还要谢谢方老师推荐。
examples.trans: It feels great, and I also want to thank Professor Fang for the recommendation.

examples.text: 这是还要。
examples.trans: This is 还要.

examples.text: 我们不用电脑，一直用这个大纸本子记账。
examples.trans: We do not use a computer; we always use this big paper ledger to keep accounts.

examples.text: 这个木头小火车是老木匠专门为孩子们做的礼物。
examples.trans: This little wooden train is a gift made specially for the children by the old carpenter.

meanings.note: Pinyin: zhèr. Spoken variant of 这里 ('here').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 没错！你已经很习惯这儿了。
examples.trans: Exactly! You already fit right in here.

meanings.note: Pinyin: jìn lái. Friendly invitation 请进来 ('please come in').

examples.text: 等星期五中午箱子主人进来，我一定坐第一排看！
examples.trans: When the suitcase owner walks in Friday at noon, I am sitting in the front row!

examples.text: 晚上好！先生，快进来避避雨吧。
examples.trans: Good evening! Sir, come inside quickly out of the rain.

meanings.note: Verb/noun yāoqǐng ('invite').

examples.text: 这次盛典必须要邀请辛惠美。
examples.trans: We definitely must invite Xin Huimei to this gala.

examples.text: 钱一到位，我们邀请她就没有障碍了。
examples.trans: Once payment clears, inviting her faces no obstacle.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà. Distal demonstrative before measure words (那个 'that one'); at clause start, means 'then / well then'.

examples.text: 那是什么铃声？有人按了两下！
examples.trans: What was that bell sound? Somebody rang twice!

examples.text: 那里没人。那是四号房的门铃。
examples.trans: Nobody is there. That is the buzzer from room four.

meanings.note: Pinyin: nà tóu. Colloquial locative noun ('the far end / across'), contrasting with 这头 ('this end').

examples.text: 哪怕坐在阳光房那头，也能听清钢琴的旋律。
examples.trans: Even sitting at the far end of the sunroom, you can hear the piano melody clearly.

examples.text: 老陈在走廊那头喊我们过去帮忙扶书架。
examples.trans: From the other end of the corridor, Chen called us over to help steady the bookcase.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lín jū. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位邻居 ('a neighbor').

examples.text: 超过八十年的小院建筑，只要一楼每天服务街坊邻居，禁止改成私人办公室。
examples.trans: Any courtyard building over eighty years old may not become private offices as long as the ground floor serves neighbours daily.

examples.text: 每天服务街坊邻居——就像对公众开放的早间咖啡馆？！
examples.trans: Serves neighbours daily—like a morning café open to the public?!

meanings.note: Pinyin: dōu. Summarizes everything BEFORE it and always stands directly before the verb/adjective (我们都喜欢).

examples.text: 谢谢！我们平时都直接叫名字吗？
examples.trans: Thank you! Do we usually just call each other by name here?

examples.text: 小美跟这条街上所有人说话都像老朋友。
examples.trans: Mei talks to everyone on this street like old friends.

meanings.note: Pinyin: lǐ. Measure word (量词): 个 (gè), e.g. 里面 ('the inside').

examples.text: 在抽屉里。我们这儿用这个大纸本子和铅笔。
examples.trans: In the drawer. Here we use this big paper ledger and a pencil.

examples.text: 在您的外套口袋里吗？
examples.trans: Are they in your coat pocket?

meanings.note: Pinyin: mén pái. Combines 门 ('door/gate') + 牌 ('numbered plaque/plate'); measure word: 块 (kuài) or 个 (gè).

examples.text: 小晴惊讶地认出他来：“您是梧桐巷十号门牌小提琴店的老邻居？！”
examples.trans: Qing recognized him in surprise: 'Are you our old neighbour from the violin shop at number ten Wutong Lane?!'

examples.text: 老陈把擦得干干净净的铜门牌端端正正钉在大门旁边。
examples.trans: Chen nailed the freshly polished brass doorplate squarely beside the front gate.

meanings.note: Pinyin: wèn. Everyday verb for asking a question (请问 'may I ask').

examples.text: 等等——先生您好！您问那个深蓝色行李箱吗？
examples.trans: Wait—hello, sir! Are you asking about that dark-blue suitcase?

examples.text: 快问他叫什么名字！记下来！
examples.trans: Quick, ask him what his name is! Write it down!

meanings.note: Pinyin: gé. Describes being separated by a wall, door, or interval of time (隔着).

examples.text: 小时候就住隔两条街。星期五对我来说……是重要日子。
examples.trans: Two streets over, when I was little. Friday for me... is an important day.

examples.text: 说这话的人每隔三十秒就扒着窗帘偷看一次！
examples.trans: Says the man peeking through the window curtain every thirty seconds!

meanings.note: Pinyin: miàn bāo shī. Measure word (量词): 位 (wèi), e.g. 一位面包师 ('a baker').

examples.text: 看下一张：请给面包师和老师留两把角落的椅子。
examples.trans: Look at the next one: 'Please save two corner chairs for the baker and the teacher.'

examples.text: 这家店的面包师每天四点起床。
examples.trans: The baker at this shop gets up at four every day.

meanings.note: Pinyin: yīn yuè. Measure word (量词): 首 (shǒu), e.g. 一首音乐 ('a piece of music').

examples.text: 一点回声也没有！木头和玻璃让音乐更好听。
examples.trans: No echo at all! Wood and glass make music sound even better.

examples.text: 每个星期五六点！整条街的人都来这儿喝茶听音乐！
examples.trans: Every Friday at six! People from the whole street came here for tea and music!

related.gloss: a piece of music (measure word 首)

首.gloss: measure word for songs and poems

meanings.en: measure word for songs and poems
meanings.note: Pinyin: shǒu. Counts songs, poems, and pieces of music (一首歌 'a song').

examples.text: 老陈，好好修一次老钢琴，它会记得每一首歌。
examples.trans: Chen, repair an old piano properly once, and it will remember every song.

examples.text: 宋老师给我们弹了一首老歌。
examples.trans: Teacher Song played an old song for us.

meanings.note: Pinyin: huáng. Describes yellow flowers, brass, or butter.

examples.text: 篮子里正躺着六个黄柠檬呢——厨房就等今天了！
examples.trans: Six yellow lemons are sitting in my basket right now—this kitchen was waiting for today!

examples.text: 秋天到了，院子里的树叶黄了。
examples.trans: Autumn has arrived, and the courtyard leaves have turned yellow.
